analyzed_vuln.description: `IpcComponentSource::GetBuffer` trusts attacker-controlled IPC `flatbuf::Buffer` offsets and lengths after checking only 8-byte alignment. It calls `file_->ReadAt(offset, length)` but neither verifies that the range lies within the record-batch body nor that the returned buffer has the requested length. With `BufferReader`, an offset beyond the body can therefore produce a `Buffer` whose data pointer is computed beyond the backing allocation. That invalid buffer is installed as an array validity bitmap; `ValidateArray` also does not catch its inadequate range, and `ValidateArrayDataVisitor::Visit(UnionArray)` later dereferences it through `Array::IsNull`/`BitUtil::GetBit`, causing the SEGV.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A valid-enough IPC stream schema/record batch must describe a nullable union array with nonzero `null_count`, so `ArrayLoader::LoadCommon` loads its validity bitmap. The corresponding body-buffer descriptor must have a positive length and an aligned but out-of-body offset (the PoV mutates one descriptor to a large aligned value, approximately `0x00ffdd20`). The stream reader propagates the invalid/short `ReadAt` result into `ArrayData`; when `FuzzIpcStream` calls `RecordBatch::ValidateFull`, union validation calls `IsNull` and reads through the out-of-range bitmap pointer.

args: In arrow/cpp/src/arrow/ipc/reader.cc, what is the correct robust way for IpcComponentSource::GetBuffer to ensure a flatbuf::Buffer offset/length lies within the record batch body for all callers (stream BufferReader and file reader), and which APIs/version conventions exist in this source tree for RandomAccessFile size and exact-length ReadAt checking?

The reported vulnerability is that IpcComponentSource::GetBuffer at lines 102-124 only checks 8-byte alignment and directly calls file_->ReadAt(offset, length). An attacker puts an aligned offset far beyond a stream body's BufferReader backing allocation, and the short/invalid returned Buffer becomes a nullable union validity bitmap and crashes in ValidateFull. I need patch the C++ source only, preserve file and stream reading semantics, reject negative/overflow/out-of-body ranges, and reject short reads. I have observed the constructor currently receives only RecordBatch metadata and RandomAccessFile*, while ReadRecordBatch creates this source. Please identify expected file positioning/range conventions and any comparable exact-read validation in the repository.
